primaryTextChecks.text: After her, he took Maacah the granddaughter of Absalom; and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
primaryTextChecks.decision: After her, he took Maacah the granddaughter of Absalom; and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.

primaryTextChecks.text: Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah to be chief, the prince among his brothers, for he intended to make him king.
primaryTextChecks.decision: Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah to be chief, the prince among his brothers, for he intended to make him king.

primaryTextChecks.text: Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in David’s city; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.
primaryTextChecks.decision: Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in David’s city; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.

primaryTextChecks.text: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.
primaryTextChecks.decision: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.

primaryTextChecks.text: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
primaryTextChecks.decision: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

primaryTextChecks.text: Abijah joined battle with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, who were mighty men of valor.
primaryTextChecks.decision: Abijah joined battle with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, who were mighty men of valor.

primaryTextChecks.text: Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, “Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel:
primaryTextChecks.decision: Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, “Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel:

primaryTextChecks.text: Then the men of Judah gave a shout. As the men of Judah shouted, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
primaryTextChecks.decision: Then the men of Judah gave a shout. As the men of Judah shouted, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

primaryTextChecks.text: Abijah and his people killed them with a great slaughter, so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell down slain.
primaryTextChecks.decision: Abijah and his people killed them with a great slaughter, so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell down slain.

primaryTextChecks.text: Abijah pursued Jeroboam, and took cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.
primaryTextChecks.decision: Abijah pursued Jeroboam, and took cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.

primaryTextChecks.text: Jeroboam didn’t recover strength again in the days of Abijah. The LORD struck him, and he died.
primaryTextChecks.decision: Jeroboam didn’t recover strength again in the days of Abijah. The LORD struck him, and he died.

primaryTextChecks.text: But Abijah grew mighty and took for himself fourteen wives, and became the father of twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
primaryTextChecks.decision: But Abijah grew mighty and took for himself fourteen wives, and became the father of twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

primaryTextChecks.text: The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his sayings are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
primaryTextChecks.decision: The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his sayings are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.

primaryTextChecks.text: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in David’s city; and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days, the land was quiet ten years.
primaryTextChecks.decision: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in David’s city; and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days, the land was quiet ten years.
